metadata.title: High-Dimensional Graphs and Variable Selection with the Lasso

nodes.name: Conditional independence graph
nodes.statement: For $X = (X_1,\dots,X_p) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)$ with nonsingular $\Sigma$, the graph $G=(\Gamma,E)$ has $\Gamma=\{1,\dots,p\}$ and $(a,b)\in E$ iff $X_a$ and $X_b$ are conditionally dependent given $X_{\Gamma\setminus\{a,b\}}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the Gaussian graphical model whose edges encode conditional dependencies; absent edges correspond to zeros in the inverse covariance matrix.

nodes.name: Neighborhood of a node
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{ne}_a$ is the smallest subset of $\Gamma\setminus\{a\}$ such that $X_a$ is conditionally independent of all remaining variables given $X_{\mathrm{ne}_a}$. Equivalently $\mathrm{ne}_a = \{b\in\Gamma\setminus\{a\}: (a,b)\in E\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The neighborhood is the smallest separating set of node a in the conditional independence graph.

nodes.name: Optimal prediction coefficients $\theta^a$
nodes.statement: $\theta^a := \arg\min_{\theta:\theta_a=0} \, E\bigl(X_a - \sum_{k\in\Gamma(n)} \theta_k X_k\bigr)^2$. The set of nonzero coefficients of $\theta^a$ equals $\mathrm{ne}_a$, and $\theta^a_b = -K_{ab}/K_{aa}$ with $K=\Sigma^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Defines the population-optimal linear-prediction coefficients of $X_a$ from the other variables; their support is exactly the neighborhood of $a$.

nodes.name: Restricted optimal coefficients $\theta^{a,A}$
nodes.statement: For $A\subseteq \Gamma(n)\setminus\{a\}$, $\theta^{a,A} := \arg\min_{\theta:\theta_k=0\,\forall k\notin A} \, E\bigl(X_a - \sum_k \theta_k X_k\bigr)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Population coefficients of the best linear predictor of $X_a$ using only variables in the index set $A$.

nodes.name: Lasso neighborhood estimate
nodes.statement: $\hat\theta^{a,\lambda} := \arg\min_{\theta:\theta_a=0}\bigl(n^{-1}\|\mathbf{X}_a - \mathbf{X}\theta\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\theta\|_1\bigr)$ and $\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}_a^{\lambda} = \{b\in\Gamma(n):\hat\theta^{a,\lambda}_b \neq 0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimates the neighborhood of node a via the supports of the Lasso regression of $X_a$ on the remaining variables.

nodes.name: Disturbed neighborhood $\mathrm{ne}_a(\eta)$
nodes.statement: $\theta^a(\eta) := \arg\min_{\theta:\theta_a=0} E\bigl(X_a - \sum_k \theta_k X_k\bigr)^2 + \eta\|\theta\|_1$, and $\mathrm{ne}_a(\eta) := \{k:\theta^a_k(\eta)\neq 0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Population-Lasso analog of the neighborhood, used to define neighborhood stability.

nodes.name: Sign-overlap quantity $S_a(b)$
nodes.statement: $S_a(b) := \sum_{k\in\mathrm{ne}_a} \mathrm{sign}(\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k)\,\theta^{b,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k$ for $a,b\in\Gamma(n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Signed inner product between the in-neighborhood coefficients of $a$ and $b$; controls the irrepresentable-type condition.

nodes.name: Edge-set estimates $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$ and $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$
nodes.statement: $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge} = \{(a,b): a\in\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_b \wedge b\in\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a\}$ and $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee} = \{(a,b): a\in\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_b \vee b\in\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two natural ways to combine per-node Lasso neighborhood estimates into a global edge set: AND vs OR aggregation.

nodes.name: Connectivity component $C_a$
nodes.statement: $C_a \subseteq \Gamma(n)$ is the set of nodes connected to $a$ by a chain of edges in $G$; $\hat C_a^\lambda$ denotes the analogous component in the estimated graph $(\Gamma,\hat E^\lambda)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The connected component of node a in the true / estimated graph.

nodes.name: Partial correlation $\pi_{ab}$
nodes.statement: $\pi_{ab}$ is the correlation between $X_a$ and $X_b$ after eliminating the linear effects of $\{X_k: k\in\Gamma(n)\setminus\{a,b\}\}$. Satisfies $\pi_{ab} = \theta^a_b\bigl(\mathrm{Var}(X_a|X_{\Gamma\setminus\{a\}})\mathrm{Var}(X_b|X_{\Gamma\setminus\{b\}})\bigr)^{1/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard partial-correlation definition used to formulate the lower-bound assumption on edge strengths.

nodes.name: Assumption 1 -- High-dimensionality
nodes.statement: There exists $\gamma>0$ such that $p(n) = O(n^{\gamma})$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Assumption 2 -- Nonsingularity / bounded conditional variance
nodes.statement: For all $a\in\Gamma(n)$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $\mathrm{Var}(X_a)=1$, and there exists $v^2>0$ with $\mathrm{Var}(X_a|X_{\Gamma(n)\setminus\{a\}}) \geq v^2$.

nodes.name: Assumption 3 -- Sparsity
nodes.statement: There exists $0\le\kappa<1$ such that $\max_{a\in\Gamma(n)} |\mathrm{ne}_a| = O(n^\kappa)$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Assumption 4 -- Bounded $\ell_1$-norm of neighborhood-restricted coefficients
nodes.statement: There exists $\vartheta<\infty$ such that for all neighboring $a,b\in\Gamma(n)$ and all $n$, $\|\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_b\setminus\{a\}}\|_1 \le \vartheta$.

nodes.name: Assumption 5 -- Magnitude of partial correlations
nodes.statement: There exist $\delta>0$ and $\xi>\kappa$ such that for every $(a,b)\in E$, $|\pi_{ab}| \ge \delta n^{-(1-\xi)/2}$.

nodes.name: Assumption 6 -- Neighborhood stability
nodes.statement: There exists $\delta<1$ such that for all $a,b\in\Gamma(n)$ with $b\notin\mathrm{ne}_a$, $|S_a(b)| < \delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: An irrepresentable-type condition controlling the signed influence of nonneighbors through the in-neighborhood coefficients.

nodes.name: Proposition 1 -- Inconsistency of the prediction-oracle penalty
nodes.statement: Under $p(n)\to\infty$, $p(n)=o(n^\gamma)$, and $\Sigma(n)$ identity except $\Sigma_{ab}=\Sigma_{ba}=s\in(0,1)$, the prediction-oracle Lasso penalty satisfies $P(\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^{\lambda_{\mathrm{oracle}}}_a \neq \mathrm{ne}_a) \to 1$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Proposition 2 -- Stability implies $|S_a(b)|\le 1$
nodes.statement: If there exists $\eta>0$ with $\mathrm{ne}_a(\eta) = \mathrm{ne}_a(0)$, then $|S_a(b)| \le 1$ for all $b\in\Gamma(n)\setminus\mathrm{ne}_a$.

nodes.name: Proposition 3 -- Necessity of Assumption 6
nodes.statement: If there exist $a,b\in\Gamma(n)$ with $b\notin\mathrm{ne}_a$ and $|S_a(b)|>1$, then for $\lambda=\lambda_n$ as in Theorem 1, $P(\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a \subseteq \mathrm{ne}_a) \to 0$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Proposition 4 -- Necessity of $\xi>\varepsilon$ for detection
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 1 with $\vartheta<1$ in Assumption 4, if some $b\in\Gamma(n)\setminus\{a\}$ has $\pi_{ab}\neq 0$ with $|\pi_{ab}|=O(n^{-(1-\xi)/2})$ for some $\xi<\varepsilon$, then $P(b\in\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a) \to 0$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 -- Type-I-error control (no false inclusions)
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 1--6 and $\lambda_n \sim d n^{-(1-\varepsilon)/2}$ with $\kappa<\varepsilon<\xi$, there exists $c>0$ such that for all $a\in\Gamma(n)$, $P(\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a \subseteq \mathrm{ne}_a) = 1 - O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 -- Type-II-error control (no false exclusions)
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 1, for $\lambda=\lambda_n$ as in Theorem 1, there exists $c>0$ with $P(\mathrm{ne}_a \subseteq \widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a) = 1 - O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$ as $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 -- Finite-sample control of joining distinct components
nodes.statement: Under Assumptions 1--6 and the penalty $\lambda(\alpha) = \frac{2\hat\sigma_a}{\sqrt n}\,\tilde\Phi^{-1}\bigl(\frac{\alpha}{2p(n)^2}\bigr)$, $P(\exists a\in\Gamma(n): \hat C_a^\lambda \not\subseteq C_a) \le \alpha$ for every $n$.

nodes.name: Corollary 1 -- Edge-set consistency
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem 2, there exists $c>0$ with $P(\hat E^\lambda = E) = 1 - O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$ as $n\to\infty$, for either aggregation $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$ or $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$.

nodes.name: Lemma A.1 -- KKT characterization of Lasso solutions
nodes.statement: With $G_b(\theta) = -2n^{-1}\langle \mathbf{X}_a-\mathbf{X}\theta,\mathbf{X}_b\rangle$, a vector $\hat\theta$ with $\hat\theta_k=0,\,\forall k\notin A$ solves (A.1) iff for every $b\in A$, $G_b(\hat\theta)=-\mathrm{sign}(\hat\theta_b)\lambda$ when $\hat\theta_b\neq 0$ and $|G_b(\hat\theta)|\le\lambda$ when $\hat\theta_b=0$. Moreover if $|G_b(\hat\theta)|<\lambda$ for some solution, then $\hat\theta_b=0$ in every solution.
conclusions: Sign-and-magnitude KKT characterization of solutions of (A.1)
Strict-inequality uniqueness statement for vanishing components

nodes.name: Lemma A.2 -- Sign consistency of restricted Lasso
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 1, for some $c>0$ and every $a\in\Gamma(n)$, $P(\mathrm{sign}(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}_b) = \mathrm{sign}(\theta^a_b),\,\forall b\in\mathrm{ne}_a) = 1 - O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$.
conclusions: Sign agreement of the Lasso restricted to $\mathrm{ne}_a$ holds with probability $1-O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$

nodes.name: Lemma A.3 -- Tail bound on parallel-component inner product
nodes.statement: Under the conditions of Theorem 1, for any $g>0$ there exists $c>0$ such that for all $a,b\in\Gamma(n)$, $P\bigl(\sup_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}} |2n^{-1}\langle R^a_\lambda(\beta), W^{\parallel}_b\rangle|/(1+|\beta|) < g\lambda\bigr) = 1 - O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$.
conclusions: Sub-Gaussian-type uniform bound on the residual / parallel-noise inner product

nodes.name: Penalty schedule (9)
nodes.statement: $\lambda(\alpha) = \dfrac{2\hat\sigma_a}{\sqrt n}\,\tilde\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{\alpha}{2p(n)^2}\right)$, where $\tilde\Phi = 1-\Phi$ and $\hat\sigma_a^2 = n^{-1}\langle \mathbf{X}_a, \mathbf{X}_a\rangle$.

nodes.name: Lasso neighborhood selection
nodes.statement: For each node $a$, fit the $\ell_1$-penalized regression of $X_a$ on the remaining variables and read off the estimated neighborhood from the support; combine per-node estimates by AND or OR aggregation.
input: Data matrix $\mathbf{X}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p(n)}$ with columns standardized to common empirical variance
output: Estimated edge set $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$ or $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$

nodes.name: Forward-selection MLE (baseline)
nodes.statement: Greedy forward search over Gaussian graphical models adding edges until a stopping criterion is met; each step refits the MLE for $O(p^2)$ candidate models.

nodes.name: LARS for Lasso path
nodes.statement: Least-angle regression algorithm computing the full Lasso path in $O(\min\{n,p\})$ steps, each of complexity $O(np)$.

nodes.name: Covariance selection
nodes.statement: Estimate the conditional independence graph (equivalently, the zero pattern of $\Sigma^{-1}$) of a $p$-dimensional Gaussian distribution from $n$ i.i.d. observations.

nodes.name: Neighborhood selection
nodes.statement: For a node $a\in\Gamma(n)$, estimate $\mathrm{ne}_a$ from $n$ i.i.d. observations of $X\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma(n))$.

nodes.name: Random spatial graph simulation
nodes.statement: Nodes uniform in $[0,1]^2$, edges retained with probability $\varphi(d/\sqrt p)$ truncated to $\le 4$ neighbors per node, partial correlation $0.245$ on edges; compares Lasso neighborhood selection ($\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$, $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$) against forward-selection MLE for $p\in\{10,20,30\}$, $n=40$.

nodes.name: 1000-node graph estimate
nodes.statement: Spatial random graph with $1000$ nodes and $1747$ edges; with $n=600$ observations and $\alpha=0.05$, the Lasso estimate $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$ recovers $1109$ edges with only two false inclusions; analogous result for $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$ at $\alpha=0.064$.

nodes.name: Robustness to long-tailed noise
nodes.statement: Adding $0.1Z$ noise with $Z$ having $t_2$ components shifts the false-rejection rate from $0.8\%$ to $1.4\%$ for $\hat E^{\lambda,\vee}$ and from $4.8\%$ to $5.2\%$ for $\hat E^{\lambda,\wedge}$ over $10$ runs with $500$ observations.

nodes.name: Cycle-free graphs imply Assumption 6
nodes.statement: If the graph contains no cycles, the global Markov property and Gaussianity yield $|\theta^{b,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k| = \sqrt{1-v^2} < 1$, so Assumption 6 is automatically satisfied.

nodes.name: Diagonal dominance implies Assumption 6
nodes.statement: If $\Sigma^{-1}(n)$ is diagonally dominant for every $n$, then Assumption 6 holds.

nodes.name: Computational complexity
nodes.statement: The Lars-based Lasso scheme requires $O(np\min\{n,p\})$ work per node and roughly $O(p^{2+2/\gamma})$ for the whole graph when $p\sim cn^\gamma$, yielding nearly quadratic scaling for large $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: By the KKT conditions of Lemma A.1 applied to the candidate solution $(0,\tau,0,\dots)$, we show first that no Lasso solution of this form exists with $\tau\ge s$, and second that solutions with $\tau<s$ cannot be the prediction-oracle solution because perturbing along a coordinate selected by KKT activity strictly decreases the squared loss.

nodes.name: Reduce to Lasso shape $(0,\tau,0,\ldots)$
nodes.statement: Since $\theta^a = (0,s,0,\dots)$, a necessary condition for $\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a = \mathrm{ne}_a$ is that the oracle Lasso solution has the form $\hat\theta^{a,\lambda} = (0,\tau,0,\dots)$ for some $\tau\neq 0$.

nodes.name: Show $P(\exists\lambda,\tau\ge s: \hat\theta^{a,\lambda}=(0,\tau,0,\dots))\to 0$
nodes.statement: Substituting $X_1 = sX_2 + W_1$ and using KKT (Lemma A.1) reduces the event to $U_2 > \max_{k>2} U_k + (\tau-s)D$ with exchangeable $U_k = \langle W_1,X_k\rangle$; exchangeability gives $P(U_2 > \max_{k>2} U_k) = (p(n)-1)^{-1}\to 0$ and a Bernstein-type bound forces $P(D<0)\to 0$.

nodes.name: Rule out $\tau<s$ as the oracle solution
nodes.statement: Let $\tau_{\max}$ be the largest $\tau$ for which $(0,\tau,0,\dots)$ is a Lasso solution. For a small perturbation $(0,\tau_{\max}+\delta\theta,\delta\theta,0,\dots)$ given by $H_n^{-1}(1,1)^T$, the loss change is $L_\delta - L_0 = -2(s-\tau_{\max})\delta\theta + 2\delta\theta^2 < 0$ for small enough $\delta\theta>0$, contradicting prediction-optimality.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2
nodes.statement: Take subdifferentials of the population-Lasso objective; in-neighborhood KKT gives the sign equation, off-neighborhood KKT gives the bound; substituting the conditional expansion of $X_b$ in terms of $\{X_k:k\in\mathrm{ne}_a\}$ yields $\sum_{k\in\mathrm{ne}_a}\theta^{b,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k\,\mathrm{sign}(\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k) \le 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Bound $P(\widehat{\mathrm{ne}}^\lambda_a \not\subseteq \mathrm{ne}_a)$ by the failure probability of the event $E = \{\max_{k\notin\mathrm{cl}_a} |G_k(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda})| < \lambda\}$ via Lemma A.1, then for each off-neighbor $b$ decompose $G_b$ using the conditional expansion and apply Lemmas A.2 and A.1 plus Bernstein's inequality, exploiting Assumption 6 with constant $\delta<1$.

nodes.name: Reduce to gradient event $E$
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma A.1 to identify the constrained Lasso $\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}$ with the unconstrained $\hat\theta^{a,\lambda}$ on the event $E := \{\max_{k\notin\mathrm{cl}_a}|G_k(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda})|<\lambda\}$, so it suffices to bound $P(E^c)$.

nodes.name: Decompose $G_b$ via $X_b = \sum_m \theta^{b,\mathrm{ne}_a}_m X_m + V_b$
nodes.statement: Substitute the population conditional expansion (A.28) into $G_b$ and use Lemma A.2 to identify $\mathrm{sign}(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}_k) = \mathrm{sign}(\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a}_k)$ with high probability.

nodes.name: Apply Assumption 6 and Bernstein's inequality
nodes.statement: Use $|\sum_m \mathrm{sign}(\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a}_m)\theta^{b,\mathrm{ne}_a}_m| \le \delta$ from Assumption 6, then Bernstein's inequality on $|2n^{-1}\langle X_a, V_b\rangle|$ yields $P(|G_b|\ge\lambda) = O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$; Bonferroni over $b$ closes the argument.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement: Mirror the proof of Theorem 1 up to (A.27) but replace the upper bound of Assumption 6 with the assumed lower bound $|S_a(b)|>1$; then equation (A.30) gives $|G_b(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda})| \ge \delta\lambda - |2n^{-1}\langle\cdot,V_b\rangle|$ with $\delta>1$, so $P(|G_b|>\lambda)\to 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: On the event $E$ (as in Theorem 1) the constrained and unconstrained Lasso solutions agree; thus $P(\exists b\in\mathrm{ne}_a: \hat\theta^{a,\lambda}_b = 0) \le P(\exists b: \hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}_b=0) + P(E^c)$. The first term vanishes by Lemma A.2 and the second by the proof of Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Identify constrained and unconstrained Lasso on $E$
nodes.statement: Conditional on $E$, $\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda} = \hat\theta^{a,\lambda}$ are unique solutions, so a missed neighbor in $\hat\theta^{a,\lambda}$ corresponds to a missed neighbor in $\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}$.

nodes.name: Bound $P(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a,\lambda}_b = 0)$ via Lemma A.2
nodes.statement: Lemma A.2 gives sign agreement of the restricted Lasso for all $b\in\mathrm{ne}_a$ with probability $1-O(\exp(-cn^\varepsilon))$, hence in particular nonzero estimates; Bonferroni over $b\in\mathrm{ne}_a$ completes the bound.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4
nodes.statement: Following Theorem 1, on the event $E$ the constrained and full Lasso agree, so it suffices to show $P(|G_b(\hat\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a\setminus\{b\},\lambda})|<\lambda)\to 1$. Decompose $G_b$ along $W^{\parallel}_b, W^{\perp}_b$, apply Lemma A.3 and a $\chi^2$-tail argument using $|\theta^{a,\mathrm{ne}_a}_b| = O(n^{-(1-\xi)/2})$ with $\xi<\varepsilon$ to drive the bound to $0$ relative to $\lambda$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: A necessary condition for $\hat C_a^\lambda \not\subseteq C_a$ is at least one estimated edge between distinct components. Conditioning on $X_{C_a}$ makes $G_b(\hat\theta^{a,C_a,\lambda}) \sim \mathcal{N}(0, R^2/n)$ with $R^2 \le \hat\sigma_a^2$. The Gaussian tail bound $2\tilde\Phi(\sqrt n\lambda/(2\hat\sigma_a))$ together with the chosen $\lambda(\alpha)$ yields $P(|G_b|\ge\lambda)\le \alpha p(n)^{-2}$; a union bound over $a,b$ produces the claim.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.1
nodes.statement: Compute the subdifferential $D(\theta)$ of $n^{-1}\|\mathbf{X}_a-\mathbf{X}\theta\|_2^2 + \lambda\|\theta\|_1$, then $\hat\theta$ solves (A.1) iff some $d\in D(\hat\theta)$ has $d_b=0$ for all $b\in A$. The strict-inequality uniqueness statement is from Theorem 3.1 of Osborne, Presnell, Turlach (2000).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.2
nodes.statement: Reduce to a one-coordinate event by fixing $\theta_b = \beta$ to define $\tilde\theta^{a,b,\lambda}(\beta)$; for $\theta^a_b > 0$ a sign flip would require $G_b(\tilde\theta(\beta))\ge -\lambda$ for some $\beta\le 0$. Bound $G_b$ using Lemma A.1 plus a residual decomposition into $W^{\parallel}_b$ and $W^{\perp}_b$; combine Lemma A.3 with $\chi^2$-tail and Bernstein bounds. Use Assumption 5 to obtain $\theta^a_b \ge q n^{-(1-\xi)/2}$ and $\xi>\varepsilon$ to conclude.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.3
nodes.statement: Schwarz's inequality bounds the inner product by $2n^{-1/2}\|W^{\parallel}_b\|_2 \cdot n^{-1/2}\|R^a_\lambda(\beta)\|_2/(1+|\beta|)$. Monotonicity of residuals in $\lambda$ and $\chi^2_n$ tails handle the residual factor; $\sigma_b^{-2}\langle W^{\parallel}_b,W^{\parallel}_b\rangle \sim \chi^2_{|\mathrm{ne}_a|-1}$ with $|\mathrm{ne}_a| = O(n^\kappa)$ and $\varepsilon>\kappa$ control the $\|W^{\parallel}_b\|_2$ factor.
